data.claim: A failure in the redaction writer degrades to FAILED_MARKER='[REDACTED:redaction-failed]', so the redactor's own failure is committed as the visible title rather than a stable scrub.
data.falsifier: show gskip-fix-Bbd88c54354-1 shows a title that is NOT '[REDACTED:redaction-failed]'.
data.mechanism: EventLog write fail-closed path replaces every string leaf with FAILED_MARKER; the item's title/body/parent/tags become that literal marker and render verbatim in next/show.
data.probe: python3 -c 'from ddflow.core import redact_errors as RE; print(repr(RE.FAILED_MARKER))'
data.question: Why does gskip-fix-Bbd88c54354-1 render its title as '[REDACTED:redaction-failed]' in ddflow next --json?

evidence.note: R361c92685a CONFIRMED: FAILED_MARKER='[REDACTED:redaction-failed]' (ddflow/core/redact_errors.py:26) is what the fail-closed writer substitutes for every string leaf, so a failed redaction commits its own failure marker as the visible title/body/parent/tags. Probe: python3 -c 'from ddflow.core import redact_errors as RE; print(repr(RE.FAILED_MARKER))' -> '[REDACTED:redaction-failed]'.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `FAILED_MARKER` to `"[REDACTED]"` makes the failure sentinel collide with the ordinary masking placeholder, so code/tests that use `FAILED_MARKER` as the observable signal of a redaction failure are no longer specific. For example, the existing fail-closed test around `tests/test_redact_provider_keys.py:99` asserts `RE.FAILED_MARKER in raw`; after this change that assertion is satisfied by any raw JSON that contains a normal `[REDACTED]` placeholder. If the redactor successfully masks the provider key (writing `[REDACTED]`) and then raises before the event writer replaces the whole event, a partially redacted non-fail-closed payload can still pass `key not in raw and RE.FAILED_MARKER in raw`, whereas the old distinct marker would have made the test fail. Thus the change weakens the failure marker into a non-failure indicator and makes the fail-closed assertion vacuous for distinguishing failure from ordinary redaction.

data.probe: The collision is the DESIGNED outcome of Befd5e5baa3: a failed redaction must degrade to the one stable placeholder every redaction path already recognises, specifically so it never surfaces a distinct 'redaction-failed' marker. The security assertion is 'key not in raw' (unchanged, still the leak check); 'RE.FAILED_MARKER in raw' now asserts the scrub-to-stable-placeholder property that the change itself introduces. fail_closed_text() returns ('[REDACTED]', 1): a bare '[REDACTED]' (whole text, count 1) is still distinguishable from a successful mask 'key [REDACTED]' which keeps context, so the nil-return unit assertion clean == RE.FAILED_MARKER stays specific. New regression test test_a_failed_redaction_scrubs_to_the_stable_placeholder_not_a_failure_marker pins the value directly.
